thread:
anya: Quick postmortem follow-up from last night's dedicated pool isolation for AcmeCorp. Root cause narrowed to peering + on-prem routing mismatch. Postmortem: <https://redwood.internal/postmortems/pc-2025-01-acme|pc-2025-01-acme>.
incident-bot: postmortem published by @anya — link above.
mike: ack, thanks. Which action items are still open?
anya: Open items I have now:
  - ACTION-231: network remediation (owner: @mike)
  - ACTION-232: on-prem checklist & runbook update (owner: @janet)
  - ACTION-233: monitoring/automated route health (owner: @kevin)
janet: quick Q — the on-prem side was NAT + stale routes? want the exact failure mode before I update the checklist.
rohith: short answer: asymmetric routing from a misconfigured peering policy + BGP community stripping on the customer's edge. Packets left via peering but return path went via on-prem NAT, so KV cache replication timed out.
kevin: mitigation we can push now: add a short-lived proxy healthcheck in the dedicated pool to surface route flaps earlier, and set a circuit-breaker to cut traffic to affected nodes. Low-risk, can be staged.
mike: I can own the network remediation. Targeting full fix and rollout by 2025-02-03. Will need help from SRE for canary.
janet: I'll update the runbook and add an "on-prem peering sanity" checklist. Can you paste the checklist here, @anya? I'll convert to playbook steps.
anya: pasted checklist below for runbook (feel free to edit):
```
- Verify BGP neighbor sessions and advertised prefixes (on-prem and cloud side)
- Confirm BGP community handling and no stripping rules
- Validate return path symmetry with traceroutes from multiple subnets
- Ensure on-prem NAT rules do not rewrite peer-to-peer traffic
- Validate KV cache replication under asymmetric path (test harness)
- Post-change: run smoke traffic through canary pool, monitor 1m latency and error spike thresholds
```
janet: :thumbsup: I'll turn that into a step-by-step and include commands we can run on customer edge. Do we want this as a separate KB or appended to the peering runbook?
anya: append to peering runbook and create a short KB for customers outlining the minimum on-prem config. Tracking in Jira epic INF-4567.
rohith: note: this pattern has shown up in two other Dedicated customers last 6 months. Recommend quarterly "peering audit" for all Dedicated on-prem customers and add a test that simulates return-path asymmetry.
kevin: also adding automated route-health alarms to dedicated monitoring. Will create an alert (route-flap-rate > 5/min) and assign to eng-sre oncall.
mike: confirmed: network fix + canary by 2025-02-03, runbook update by 2025-01-20, monitoring in place by 2025-01-31. I'll file the milestone in INF-4567 today.
anya: thanks everyone — I'll update the postmortem with owners, deadlines, and link INF-4567. Weekly status check-in on Tuesdays; I'll ping this thread with progress notes. If anyone needs a temp owner swap, shout here.
kevin: noted, will start alert PR this week.
janet: I'll start drafting the KB and share a draft by Friday.
mike: good.
anya: closing for now — will reopen thread when I update the postmortem. :wave:
